subtitle: On the Windswept Plateau Where Many Styles Met the Sun

panels.shot: epic wide shot from above the plateau at sunrise
panels.action: The Spirit of Martand Sun Temple rises ghostlike from ruined trefoil arches on a high Kashmiri plateau, bathed in cold dawn light with distant snow peaks framing the silent limestone courts.

dialogue.text: On a high plateau above the valley, Lalitaditya’s Martand rose in stone to the sun—built in a style no one had seen before, fated to be shattered and yet never truly erased.

i18n.hi: घाटी से ऊपर ऊँचे पठार पर, ललितादित्य का मार्तंड सूर्य तक पत्थर में उठा—ऐसे रूप में जो पहले कभी न देखा गया, टूटने को नियति था, मिटने को नहीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward the plateau from the valley floor
panels.action: From the lush Kashmir valley below, the camera looks up at the long ridge of Martand, its ruined walls etched against the sky as the Spirit of Martand hovers, half-formed, over scattered limestone blocks.

dialogue.text: Kalhana’s chronicle names a king, Lalitaditya Muktapida, and a great sun shrine at Martand. The ruins still stand, but the age that shaped them feels like another world.

i18n.hi: कल्हण की राजतरंगिणी एक राजा, ललितादित्य मुक्तापीड, और मार्तंड में महान सूर्य मंदिर का ज़िक्र करती है। खंडहर आज भी हैं, पर जिसने इन्हें गढ़ा वह युग किसी और ही दुनिया जैसा लगता है।

panels.shot: wide shot imagining the plateau in the 8th century, fade overlay with spirit
panels.action: The plateau appears as it might have in the 8th century—bare rock, scattered workers’ huts—while the Spirit of Martand reaches out, as if guiding invisible hands that mark lines on the ground.

dialogue.text: Around 724–760 CE, under the Karkota rulers, Kashmir’s craftsmen faced a daring commission: not just another shrine, but a vast stone complex to the sun on open, windswept rock.

i18n.hi: ७२४–७६० ई. के बीच कार्कोट शासकों के दौर में, कश्मीर के शिल्पियों के सामने दुस्साहस खड़ा था: बस एक और मंदिर नहीं, खुली, तूफ़ानी चट्टान पर सूर्य का विराट पत्थर नगर।

panels.shot: architectural bird’s-eye over the ground plan taking shape
panels.action: Marks in the earth form a great rectangle; lines show the central shrine, a surrounding peristyle and an eastern gateway, while the Spirit of Martand hovers above like a translucent plan come to life.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists later traced the plan: a grand courtyard, an axial eastern gateway, a cloister of cells and a towering central cella. It was a Kashmiri temple on an almost royal scale.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्वविदों ने बाद में नक्शा पढ़ा: विशाल प्रांगण, पूर्व की ओर सीधा द्वार, कोठरियों की परिक्रमा और बीच में अटारीनुमा गर्भगृह। यह कश्मीरी मंदिर था, लगभग राजदरबार के पैमाने पर।

panels.shot: medium shot of limestone blocks being quarried and ferried
panels.action: Workers wrestle massive limestone blocks from the hillside, sledging them across rollers, while the Spirit of Martand watches, its form shimmering within the pale stone surfaces.

dialogue.text: They chose limestone—hard, pale, unforgiving. Each block had to be cut, dressed and set with care, or the weight of Martand would crack its own bones.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने चुना चूनापत्थर—सख़्त, फीका, बेरहम। हर गारे को काटना, तराशना, जमाना पड़ता, वरना मार्तंड का बोझ उसी की हड्डियाँ चटका देता।

panels.shot: close-up on emerging trefoil arch carving
panels.action: A sculptor’s hands carve a graceful trefoil curve into a stone frame; behind him, the Spirit of Martand flows through repeated arches rising in a rhythm along a wall.

dialogue.text: Along the walls, a new sign appeared: trefoil arches, repeated with care. Their curve echoed Gandhara and the western regions, but their rhythm would become distinctly Kashmiri.

i18n.hi: दीवारों के साथ एक नया चिह्न उभरा: त्रिपत्र मेहराबें, बार-बार सँवारी हुई। उनकी वक्रता गंधार और पश्चिम की याद दिलाती, पर उनकी लय धीरे-धीरे कश्मीरी हो चली।

panels.shot: low-angle interior wide of the central shrine under construction
panels.action: The skeletal shell of the central shrine towers above scaffolding, massive pilasters and niches rising tier upon tier as the Spirit of Martand stands within, arms outstretched to the sky opening above.

dialogue.text: Percy Brown saw in these walls a synthesis: North Indian temple massing, Gandharan influences, local Kashmiri solutions to snow, wind and light. The Martand shrine was engineering as devotion.

i18n.hi: पर्सी ब्राउन ने इन दीवारों में एक संगम देखा: उत्तर भारतीय मंदिर की देह, गंधार की छाप, और बर्फ़, हवा, रोशनी के लिए कश्मीरी उपाय। मार्तंड का मंदिर भक्ति जितना ही अभियान्त्रिकी था।

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of completed courtyard with peristyle and gateway
panels.action: The Martand complex stands complete: a broad courtyard ringed by a cloister of stone cells, dominated by the tall central shrine, with an imposing eastern gateway framing the rising sun as the Spirit of Martand shines within.

dialogue.text: When the last block settled and the scaffolds fell away, a new Kashmiri vocabulary stood in stone: courts and cloisters, axial gateways, trefoil frames and lofty walls catching the highland light.

i18n.hi: आख़िरी पत्थर जड़ते ही और मचान गिरते ही, पत्थर में एक नई कश्मीरी भाषा खड़ी हो गई: आँगन और परिक्रमा, सीध में खुलते द्वार, त्रिपत्र चौखटें, और ऊँची दीवारें जो पहाड़ी रोशनी पकड़ती थीं।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of dawn ritual in the courtyard
panels.action: At sunrise, priests and courtiers gather in the courtyard before the central shrine, smoke from lamps curling upward as the first light floods through the eastern gateway and around the luminous Spirit of Martand.

dialogue.text: Kalhana calls it a shrine of Aditya. In its courts the first beams of the sun poured through the eastern gate, washing walls and faces alike in a ritual of light and stone.

i18n.hi: कल्हण इसे आदित्य का देवालय कहते हैं। इसके प्रांगण में सूरज की पहली किरणें पूर्वी द्वार से झरतीं, दीवारों और चेहरों पर समान रूप से बहतीं—रोशनी और पत्थर की रोज़ की पूजा।

panels.shot: slow tracking shot along the peristyle cells
panels.action: The camera glides along the shaded peristyle; stone doorways open into small cells while the Spirit of Martand moves as a warm glow through the colonnade, hinting at quiet worship and shelter.

dialogue.text: Behind the spectacle lay function. The peristyle’s many cells held images, offerings and devotees, turning Martand from a single shrine into a small stone city of worship.

i18n.hi: इस दृश्य के पीछे उपयोग छिपा था। परिक्रमा की कोठरियों में मूर्तियाँ, भेंटें और साधक ठहरते, और मार्तंड एक अकेले मंदिर से बढ़कर पत्थर की छोटी नगर-तीर्थ बन जाता।

panels.shot: composed wide shot linking Martand to other Kashmiri temples
panels.action: Martand’s forms echo across the landscape as ghostly overlays of other Kashmiri temples—smaller shrines, trefoil arches, colonnades—while the Spirit of Martand stands central, radiating architectural influence.

dialogue.text: Later shrines across Kashmir echoed Martand’s choices. Trefoil arches, high platforms, cloistered courts—what began on this plateau became a template for an entire region’s sacred stone.

i18n.hi: बाद के कश्मीरी मंदिरों ने मार्तंड की पसंद दोहराई। त्रिपत्र मेहराबें, ऊँचे चबूतरे, घिरी हुई परिक्रमा—जो इस पठार पर शुरू हुआ, वही पूरे क्षेत्र का पवित्र पत्थर मानक बन गया।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing centuries passing over the plateau
panels.action: Clouds race, snow falls and melts, grass grows around the temple as the structure weathers; the Spirit of Martand dims slightly but remains present among the ageing stones.

dialogue.text: Centuries turned. Dynasties rose and fell in the valley below, but on the high ridge the limestone held its form, the trefoil arches still catching sun and storm.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बदलीं। घाटी में वंश उठे और ढहे, पर ऊँची कगार पर चूनापत्थर अपनी सूरत थामे रहा, त्रिपत्र मेहराबें अब भी सूरज और तूफ़ान को जकड़ती रहीं।

panels.shot: somber wide shot suggesting the moment of destruction without violence
panels.action: The temple stands under a darkened sky; tools and men approach its walls, some stones lie toppled, while the Spirit of Martand recoils, its glowing form splintered but not extinguished.

dialogue.text: Later chroniclers like Jonaraja, writing of Sultan Sikandar Shah Miri in the late 14th–early 15th century, speak of temples broken, Martand among them, amid campaigns of power and change.

i18n.hi: जोनराज जैसे बाद के लेखक, जो चौदहवीं–पंद्रहवीं सदी की शुरुआत में सुल्तान सिकंदर शाह मिरी के बारे में लिखते हैं, टूटते मंदिरों की बातें करते हैं—मार्तंड भी उनमें है—ताक़त और बदलाव की मुहिमों के बीच।

panels.shot: closer shot on collapsed walls and surviving arches
panels.action: Many walls lie fallen in ordered heaps, yet sections of the towering central façade and trefoil arches still stand stark against the sky, and the Spirit of Martand gathers itself within the remaining stone.

dialogue.text: The shrine’s roof fell; parts of its walls were cast down. But the main façade, the rhythm of its arches and the sweep of the courtyard endured as ruins rather than as a living temple.

i18n.hi: देवालय की छत गिरी; दीवारों के हिस्से ढहा दिए गए। पर मुख्य अग्रभाग, मेहराबों की लय और आँगन की चौड़ाई ज़िंदा मंदिर नहीं, खंडहर के रूप में फिर भी टिकी रही।

panels.shot: documentary-style medium wide of modern archaeologists among ruins
panels.action: Modern archaeologists move carefully through Martand’s ruins, measuring, sketching and studying blocks as the Spirit of Martand hovers above a drawn plan spread on a board.

dialogue.text: When Stein, Brown and others mapped Martand, they read not only loss but design: the precise courtyard plan, the engineering of its cloister, the calculated play of sun and shadow on stone.

i18n.hi: जब स्टाइन, ब्राउन और दूसरे विद्वानों ने मार्तंड का नक्शा बनाया, उन्होंने सिर्फ़ क्षति नहीं, योजना भी पढ़ी: प्रांगण की सटीक रचना, परिक्रमा की कारीगरी, और पत्थर पर सूरज–छाया की सोची-समझी चाल।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of the Spirit of Martand touching weathered stone
panels.action: The Spirit of Martand lays a hand on a weathered trefoil frame, its luminous fingers tracing cracks and moss as distant pilgrims stand in quiet reflection beyond.

dialogue.speaker: the_martand_sun_temple
dialogue.text: I was raised where many paths met, and so I endure in many memories.

i18n.hi: मैं वहाँ पला जहाँ कई राहें मिलती थीं, इसलिए मैं कई यादों में टिक गया हूँ।

panels.shot: final wide shot at sunset, temple ruins and valley stretching beyond
panels.action: At sunset, Martand’s ruins glow in warm light, their silhouette clear against the sky; the Spirit of Martand stands tall within the broken shrine, looking out over the Kashmir valley below.

dialogue.text: Martand’s courts no longer ring with ritual, yet its broken arches still teach how one age fused distant styles into a new Kashmiri form, leaving innovation in stone long after empire and idol were gone.

i18n.hi: मार्तंड के प्रांगण अब अनुष्ठान की गूँज से खाली हैं, पर उसकी टूटी मेहराबें आज भी दिखाती हैं कि एक युग ने दूर-दूर की शैलियाँ जोड़कर एक नई कश्मीरी सूरत गढ़ी—नवाचार को पत्थर में छोड़कर, बहुत बाद तक जब साम्राज्य और मूर्तियाँ दोनों जा चुके थे।

title_i18n.en: The Sun Temple on the High Plateau

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Windswept Plateau Where Many Styles Met the Sun
subtitle_i18n.hi: उस बयाबान पठार पर जहाँ कई धाराएँ सूर्य से मिलीं
